stem: In a two-tier spine-leaf fabric, a host on one leaf sends a frame to a host on a different leaf. How many spine switches does that traffic cross?
explanation: Every leaf is cabled to every spine and there are no spine-to-spine links, so a leaf-to-leaf path is exactly two hops: leaf to one spine and back down to the other leaf. Which spine is chosen is decided per flow by equal-cost multipathing, but it is always a single spine for that flow.

choices.text: Exactly one, because the path is leaf to one spine and back down to the other leaf
Every spine in the fabric, because the frame is flooded to all of them
Zero, because leaf switches are directly cabled to each other
Two, because the fabric always traverses a primary and a backup spine

stem: Which term describes the coverage area of a single access point radio, within which a client can associate and pass traffic?
explanation: The basic service area is the physical footprint of one AP radio cell. The basic service set is the set of stations inside it, the BSSID names that AP radio, and an extended service set is several BSAs joined by the distribution system.

choices.text: Basic service area (BSA)
Extended service set (ESS)
Basic service set identifier (BSSID)
Distribution system (DS)

stem: How many usable host addresses does an IPv4 /30 subnet provide?
explanation: A /30 leaves two host bits, so the block holds four addresses. One is the network address and one is the broadcast, which leaves two usable addresses. That is why /30 is popular on point-to-point links.

stem: Which device sits in a hardened segment and is the only host administrators may log into before reaching servers in a protected internal network?
explanation: A bastion host, also called a jump host, is deliberately exposed and hardened so it can be the single controlled entry point for management access. Administrators hop through it into the protected network, so the internal servers never accept direct administrative sessions from untrusted networks.

choices.text: A bastion (jump) host
An inline intrusion prevention system
A server load balancer
A Layer 2 access switch

stem: TIA/EIA structured cabling limits a horizontal copper cable run from the telecommunications room to the work area outlet to what maximum length?
explanation: The permanent link is capped at 90 m. The 10 m of patch cords at the two ends bring the full channel to the familiar 100 m limit, which is why the two numbers are often confused.

stem: In a fiber-optic cable, what is the function of the cladding around the core?
explanation: The core has the higher refractive index and the cladding the lower one. Light arriving at that boundary at a shallow angle is totally internally reflected back into the core, which is what turns the fiber into a waveguide. Strength members and buffers protect the cable but do not guide light.

choices.text: It has a lower refractive index than the core, so light is reflected back into the core
It provides a metallic shield that blocks electromagnetic interference
It carries a second signal channel in parallel with the core
It adds tensile strength only and has no optical role

stem: A campus is being redesigned so that each building routes to the core instead of extending VLANs across the whole campus. What is the main benefit of pushing Layer 3 closer to the access layer?
explanation: Routing at each building bounds both the broadcast domain and the spanning-tree topology to that building. A loop or a broadcast storm in one closet then cannot take down a campus-wide VLAN. Extending VLANs between buildings does exactly the opposite and is what the redesign is moving away from.

choices.text: Broadcast domains stay small and a failure is contained to one building instead of a campus-wide VLAN
Every VLAN must still span the core so host addressing stays consistent
It removes the need to configure a default gateway on the hosts
It converts all access ports into trunk ports automatically

stem: A firewall is inserted into an existing subnet without readdressing any hosts or changing their default gateway. Which operating mode does this require?
explanation: In transparent mode the firewall bridges its interfaces, so it holds no address on the data path and hosts keep the same gateway. Routed mode would make the firewall the gateway and force readdressing or gateway changes; tap and promiscuous modes only observe traffic and cannot enforce policy.

choices.text: Transparent (Layer 2) mode
Routed (Layer 3) mode
Passive tap mode
Promiscuous intrusion-detection mode

stem: An access point advertises the same SSID on 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz. Clients at the far edge of the cell associate on 2.4 GHz but fail on 5 GHz. Why?
explanation: Free-space path loss rises with frequency, so at equal transmit power a 5 GHz signal simply does not travel as far and is absorbed more by walls and furnishings. Channel overlap is a 2.4 GHz problem, where only three channels do not overlap, and regulatory power limits vary by region rather than being the general cause.

choices.text: Higher frequencies attenuate faster, so 5 GHz has a smaller cell at the same transmit power
5 GHz is limited to a lower transmit power by law in every region
5 GHz channels overlap each other and interfere
5 GHz requires a stronger encryption cipher than 2.4 GHz

stem: In a spine-leaf fabric, which role does a border leaf perform?
explanation: Ordinary leafs only attach servers and storage. The border leaf provides the fabric's exit point to external networks such as a WAN router or the internet edge. The fabric is normally routed with equal-cost multipathing, so there is no spanning-tree root election and no single aggregation link.

choices.text: It connects the fabric to devices outside it, such as a WAN router or the internet edge
It is the only leaf permitted to carry storage traffic
It is elected as the spanning-tree root for the whole fabric
It aggregates all leaf-to-leaf traffic through one link

stem: An application runs as several identical instances in one public cloud region. Why should they be placed in different availability zones rather than all in one?
explanation: An availability zone is an isolated fault domain with its own power, cooling, and networking. Spreading instances across zones means a datacenter-level failure removes only part of the capacity. A region contains multiple zones, cross-zone traffic is often billed, and public addressing is not tied to zones.

choices.text: Each zone has independent power, cooling, and networking, so one zone's failure does not take down the whole application
Zones are the only place where public IP addresses can be assigned
Traffic between zones is always free of charge
A region can host instances in only one zone at a time

stem: An administrator needs a second, independently running copy of a virtual machine for a test lab. Which operation produces that?
explanation: A clone is a complete independent copy with its own virtual disks and its own lifecycle, so it can be powered on, changed, or deleted without touching the original. A snapshot, called a checkpoint in Hyper-V, captures a point in time of the existing VM for rollback and keeps sharing its disk chain.

choices.text: Cloning the virtual machine
Taking a snapshot of the virtual machine
Creating a checkpoint of the virtual machine
Exporting the virtual machine's console log

stem: Why does a modular chassis switch place the control plane on a supervisor engine that is separate from the line cards?
explanation: The line cards hold the ports and the forwarding hardware, while the supervisor runs routing, management, and the control plane once for the whole chassis. That split lets an individual card be swapped without rebuilding the control plane and lets a redundant supervisor take over. Forwarding stays in hardware on the cards rather than being switched by a central CPU.

choices.text: The supervisor runs routing and management for all line cards, so a card can be replaced without rebuilding the control plane
Line cards cannot forward frames unless the supervisor switches each frame in software
The supervisor exists only to supply power to the line cards
Each line card must run its own independent routing process with no shared state

stem: Two VPCs both use 10.0.0.0/16. A request to peer them is rejected. What is the reason?
explanation: A peering connection is a route between two private address spaces. If both sides claim 10.0.0.0/16, the routing table cannot tell which VPC owns a given address, so the provider refuses the connection. One side has to be readdressed, or the overlap must be reached through NAT or a private endpoint instead. Peering works across regions and supports IPv4.

choices.text: Peering routes between the two private ranges, so identical prefixes would make every destination ambiguous
Peering requires both VPCs to be in the same region
Peering only supports IPv6 CIDR blocks
A VPC may have at most two peering connections

stem: Storm control is configured on an interface. Which direction of traffic does it measure?
explanation: Storm control polices the rate at which broadcast, multicast, or unknown-unicast frames arrive on the port, so it measures ingress only. There is no equivalent egress counter, and the feature is about frame rates rather than interface error counters.

choices.text: Ingress only
Egress only
Both ingress and egress
Neither, because it counts interface errors instead

stem: How does a working EtherChannel bundle appear to spanning tree?
explanation: The port channel is presented to STP as one logical port. That is precisely why bundling works: the member links are not seen as parallel links, so STP does not block all but one of them.

choices.text: As a single logical link, so STP sees one port rather than the individual members
As one link per member, each in its own STP state
As a loop that STP must block
As a trunk that STP ignores completely

stem: Which statement about VLAN 1 on a Cisco switch is true?
explanation: VLAN 1 exists by default, is the default native VLAN, and carries control-plane traffic such as CDP and VTP. The CLI refuses to delete or rename it, which is why it cannot be removed like a user-created VLAN.

choices.text: It is the default VLAN and cannot be deleted
It can be deleted once another VLAN has been created
It is reserved for voice traffic only
It exists only when VTP is in server mode

stem: A PVST+ network carries VLANs 10, 20, and 30. How many root bridges exist?
explanation: PVST+ runs a separate spanning-tree instance per VLAN, and each instance elects its own root. The same physical switch often holds all three root roles by design, but conceptually there is one root per VLAN instance, not one per switch block.

choices.text: One per VLAN, so up to three
One for the whole switch block regardless of VLAN
One per access switch
None, because PVST+ uses a single shared tree

stem: Which command reports the IOS image version, the hardware model, and how long the device has been running?
explanation: `show version` prints the IOS version and image file, the platform and memory, the configuration register, and the uptime since the last reload. `show interfaces status` covers port state, `show running-config` shows the active configuration, and `show flash:` lists filesystem contents.

choices.text: `show version`
`show interfaces status`
`show running-config`
`show flash:`

stem: A frame arrives at a switch with a source MAC address that has the group (multicast) bit set. What does the switch do with that address?
explanation: A source address must be a unicast address. With the group bit set the value cannot be a real station address, so the switch refuses to learn it. That check is one small defence against poisoning the table with bogus source addresses.

choices.text: It does not add it to the MAC address table
It learns it as a normal dynamic entry
It installs it as a static entry
It floods the frame back out the receiving port

stem: When spanning tree detects a topology change, why does the switch age out dynamic MAC entries faster than the normal aging time?
explanation: A topology change means a destination that used to be reached out one port may now be out another. Shortening the aging timer forces relearning from the new topology instead of black-holing traffic toward a stale port. Memory pressure and VLAN assignment play no part in it.

choices.text: Hosts may now be reachable through a different port, so stale entries would forward frames the wrong way
The table is cleared to free memory for the new topology
Faster aging reduces the CPU cost of the STP recalculation
The entries must be removed so the switch can relearn VLAN assignments

stem: A switch stops receiving BPDUs on a port that had been its root port. What finally causes it to stop trusting the stored information?
explanation: Every BPDU refreshes the stored topology information, and max-age is the lifetime of that information, 20 seconds by default. When it expires the switch discards the old root path and recomputes. Hello is the send interval and forward delay governs the listening and learning phases.

choices.text: The max-age timer expires because no new BPDU refreshed it
The forward-delay timer expires twice in a row
The hello timer expires once
The hold-time timer expires

stem: Which command confirms that a local port is receiving LACPDUs from the expected partner and shows that partner's system ID and port state?
explanation: `show lacp neighbor` lists, per member link, the partner's system ID, port number, age, and flags. `show etherchannel summary` reports the aggregate bundle state but not the neighbour detail, and the spanning-tree and trunk commands answer different questions.

choices.text: `show lacp neighbor`
`show etherchannel summary`
`show spanning-tree interface`
`show interfaces trunk`

stem: On a virtual switch inside a hypervisor, what is the role of an uplink port?
explanation: Guest ports, grouped into port groups, attach virtual machines to the virtual switch. The uplink binds that virtual switch to a physical NIC so frames can reach the physical network. VLAN tagging and the management address are separate configuration items.

choices.text: It carries traffic from the virtual switch out to the physical network
It connects two virtual machines directly to each other
It assigns VLAN tags to virtual machine traffic
It provides the management IP address for the hypervisor

stem: An 802.1Q trunk must send the native VLAN tagged instead of untagged. Which command enables that?
explanation: `vlan dot1q tag native` is a global command that makes 802.1Q trunks tag frames in the native VLAN too, closing the untagged-native-VLAN hopping gap. Both ends must agree. `dot1q-tunnel` is QinQ, and `switchport trunk native vlan` only sets which VLAN is native.

choices.text: `vlan dot1q tag native`
`switchport trunk native vlan tag`
`switchport mode dot1q-tunnel`
`encapsulation dot1q native`

stem: A port security port serves an IP phone with a PC daisy-chained behind it. Which setting allows both devices to be learned?
explanation: One secure MAC address is the default, but a phone plus a downstream PC presents two source MAC addresses on the same port, so the maximum must be raised to at least 2. Violation mode and aging settings change what happens to a violation, not how many addresses may be learned.

choices.text: `switchport port-security maximum 2`
`switchport port-security maximum 1`
`switchport port-security violation protect`
`switchport port-security aging static`

stem: Port security is enabled with a sticky MAC on an access port. An attacker on that same port copies the authorized host's MAC address. What can port security do about it?
explanation: Port security authenticates an address on a port, not a person. Once the attacker uses the permitted MAC on the permitted port, every check passes and traffic is allowed. Defending against that needs an identity-based control such as 802.1X rather than a Layer 2 address filter.

choices.text: Nothing, because the spoofed address is exactly the address the port is already configured to allow
It err-disables the port because two hosts now share one MAC
It moves the entry to a different port automatically
It converts the sticky entry to a static entry and blocks the new host

stem: Why can a switch apply an ACL to every frame at line rate without slowing down?
explanation: The ACL is compiled into ternary content-addressable memory, which compares a packet's fields against all entries in parallel in a single lookup. The result is available at forwarding speed. Sending the traffic to the CPU would be far too slow, and per-flow caching is a software firewall technique rather than how switch ACLs work.

choices.text: The ACL is compiled into ternary content-addressable memory and evaluated in hardware as the frame is forwarded
The ACL is evaluated only for the first packet of each flow and the result is cached
The switch sends all ACL-bound traffic to the CPU for a software lookup
The ACL is applied only to management traffic by design

stem: Which OSPF router type has every one of its interfaces in the same area?
explanation: An internal router keeps all interfaces in one area and therefore holds a single link-state database. An area border router straddles two or more areas, an autonomous system boundary router redistributes external routes, and a designated router is a per-segment role rather than a router classification.

choices.text: Internal router
Area border router
Autonomous system boundary router
Designated router

stem: What is the purpose of the OSPF Hello packet?
explanation: Hellos are sent on a timer so neighbours can be discovered and so each side can prove the other is still alive. The parameters inside them must match before an adjacency can form. The database description, request, update, and acknowledgment packets are the ones that carry the link-state database.

choices.text: To discover neighbours and keep the adjacency alive
To carry the full link-state database to a neighbour
To request specific LSAs from a neighbour
To acknowledge every received LSA

stem: Hosts use a first-hop redundancy virtual IP as their default gateway. Which device answers their ARP request for that IP?
explanation: The active router, called the master in VRRP, owns the virtual IP and the virtual MAC and answers ARP so hosts map the gateway to the shared MAC. If it fails, the standby takes over the same virtual MAC and hosts never notice.

choices.text: The active (master) router of the group
Every router in the group, in turn
The standby router only
The switch that hosts the SVI

stem: A routing table entry reads `O 10.5.0.0/16 [110/20] via 192.168.1.2`. What does 192.168.1.2 represent?
explanation: `via` is the next hop: the address of the adjacent router that will forward the packet, reachable over a connected subnet. The prefix is the destination, the local interface address would appear as the outgoing interface, and the router ID is a separate 32-bit identifier that never appears in this field.

choices.text: The next-hop address of the router that will forward the packet
The destination host that is being routed to
The local interface address of this router
The OSPF router ID of the neighbour

stem: Why does an area border router maintain a separate link-state database for each area it belongs to?
explanation: Topology is described per area, so each area's database covers only that area's links. The ABR keeps one database per area and injects summarized inter-area routes instead of leaking full topology across the boundary. That containment is the whole point of splitting a domain into areas.

choices.text: Each area has its own topology, so the ABR runs a separate SPF per area and summarizes between them
The ABR stores one database and filters it per area on output
OSPF requires a physically separate process for every area
All areas share one database and differ only in metric

stem: Two sources offer a route to 10.1.0.0/16: OSPF with metric 20 and EIGRP with metric 409600. Which route is installed?
explanation: Different protocols measure cost in unrelated units, so IOS first compares administrative distance: EIGRP is 90 and OSPF is 110. EIGRP therefore wins, even though its raw metric number is larger. Metrics are only compared between routes from the same protocol.

choices.text: The EIGRP route, because administrative distance is compared before metric
The OSPF route, because 20 is the lower metric
Both, because the two metrics cannot be compared
Neither, until the metrics are normalized to a common scale

stem: In EIGRP, what is the successor for a destination?
explanation: The successor is the best loop-free path, chosen by the composite metric, and it is the one installed in the routing table. A feasible successor is the loop-free backup path that is kept in the topology table and promoted if the successor fails.

choices.text: The lowest-metric loop-free path, which is installed in the routing table
Any path whose reported distance is higher than the feasible distance
The backup path that is kept only in the topology table
The neighbour with the highest interface bandwidth

stem: A router has `ip route 10.16.0.0 255.255.0.0 Null0`. What happens to a packet for 10.16.5.5 when no more specific route exists?
explanation: A static route pointing at Null0 is a discard route. Any packet that matches the summary and has no longer match is dropped. It is used to black-hole the unallocated space inside an advertised summary and so prevent routing loops.

choices.text: It is discarded, because the summary matches and Null0 drops the traffic
It is flooded out every interface
It is forwarded to the default gateway
It triggers an ICMP redirect toward the source

stem: What problem does a first-hop redundancy protocol solve?
explanation: Hosts are configured with a single default gateway address. FHRP makes that address virtual so a standby router can take it over when the active one fails, removing the gateway as a single point of failure. Spanning tree, load balancing, and admission control are separate problems.

choices.text: A host has one default gateway, so its failure would cut the host off from other subnets
It prevents spanning-tree loops between access switches
It distributes inbound traffic across several servers
It authenticates hosts before they may use the gateway

stem: A router subinterface is numbered `.30` but is configured with `encapsulation dot1q 40`. Which VLAN's traffic does it handle?
explanation: The subinterface number is only a local label. The argument to `encapsulation dot1q` is what tags and matches the traffic, so this subinterface handles VLAN 40. Mismatched numbering is confusing but functional, which is exactly why it makes a good exam trap.

choices.text: VLAN 40, because the encapsulation command supplies the VLAN ID
VLAN 30, because the subinterface number is the VLAN
Both VLAN 30 and VLAN 40
Neither, until the subinterface is renumbered to match

stem: An interface is configured with 192.168.1.1/24, and the table shows both 192.168.1.0/24 connected and 192.168.1.1/32 local. Why is the /32 entry there?
explanation: The connected route covers the whole subnet, but a packet addressed to the router's own address must be delivered locally rather than forwarded back out an interface. The /32 local route marks that address as belonging to the device, so the router punts it to itself.

choices.text: It identifies the router's own address so traffic to it is received locally instead of being forwarded
It reserves the broadcast address for the subnet
It is a leftover artifact of the ARP cache
It is the route used to reach the default gateway

stem: Why does HSRP use a virtual MAC address instead of the active router's burned-in address?
explanation: Hosts cache the gateway's MAC in their ARP table. If the group used the active router's burned-in address, a failover would change the MAC and every host would have to re-ARP before it could send. A shared virtual MAC (0000.0c07.acXX) moves with the active role, so failover is invisible to the hosts.

choices.text: So the standby can take over the same MAC and hosts need no ARP refresh or gateway change
So the virtual MAC can be routed across a WAN link
Because a burned-in address cannot legally appear in an ARP reply
Because the virtual MAC encrypts the HSRP hello messages

stem: In SNMPv2c, how is the community string sent between the manager and the agent?
explanation: Version 2c has no encryption at all. The community is a plaintext string that doubles as the access credential, which is the main reason SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy exists. Hashing and encryption belong to v3.

choices.text: In cleartext inside every request and response
Encrypted with a pre-shared key
Hashed with MD5 to form a digest
Encrypted inside a TLS tunnel

stem: What does the command `crypto key zeroize rsa` do?
explanation: `zeroize` destroys the local RSA key pair. SSH needs that key pair for its session handshake, so SSH stops working until `crypto key generate rsa` creates new keys. It has no effect on data stored on clients.

choices.text: Deletes the router's RSA key pair, which disables SSH until new keys are generated
Clears the RSA keys cached by connected SSH clients
Resets the RSA counter used for accounting
Removes the RSA signature from the running configuration only

stem: A clientless SSL VPN is reached with nothing but a web browser. Which protocol and port does the client use?
explanation: Clientless SSL VPN runs in the browser over HTTPS on TCP 443, so it needs no client software and usually passes restrictive firewalls. ESP, IKE, and L2TP belong to tunnels that require a client or a dialer.

choices.text: HTTPS over TCP 443
IPsec ESP over IP protocol 50
IKE over UDP 500
L2TP over UDP 1701

stem: On a Cisco router, when is inside source NAT applied to an outbound packet relative to the routing lookup?
explanation: IOS routes the packet first, then translates the inside source as the packet leaves the outside interface. The reverse translation on returning traffic happens on ingress, before the routing lookup. That asymmetry is why inside ACLs see pre-translation addresses while outside ACLs see post-translation addresses.

choices.text: After the routing decision, as the packet leaves the outside interface
Before routing, so the destination can be translated first
Only after the packet has been dropped for lack of a route
On the ingress interface, before any ACL is evaluated

stem: With no logging configuration at all, what is the default severity level for messages shown on the console?
explanation: `logging console` defaults to debugging, level 7, so everything from level 0 through 7 is printed. That is why a busy debug session can lock up a console session until the console logging level is raised.

choices.text: Debugging (level 7)
Informational (level 6)
Warnings (level 4)
Errors (level 3)

stem: What is the default DHCP lease duration on a Cisco IOS router acting as a DHCP server?
explanation: The default is one day. `lease infinite` exists but is not the default, and shorter leases raise the volume of renew traffic without any benefit on a stable network.

choices.text: One day
One hour
One week
Infinite

stem: Which port does IKE use to establish the phase 1 security association for an IPsec VPN?
explanation: IKE negotiates the phase 1 association over UDP 500. UDP 4500 carries NAT-traversal encapsulated ESP, and IP protocol 50 is ESP itself, which is the data path rather than the negotiation.

choices.text: UDP 500
TCP 500
UDP 4500
IP protocol 50

stem: Which reverse DNS zone name corresponds to the network 192.168.1.0/24?
explanation: Reverse zones reverse the octets of the network and append `in-addr.arpa`. So 192.168.1.0/24 becomes 1.168.192.in-addr.arpa, and the PTR records inside it are named for the final octet of each host address.

choices.text: 1.168.192.in-addr.arpa
192.168.1.in-addr.arpa
in-addr.arpa.192.168.1
1.192.168.in-addr.arpa

stem: DHCP snooping is enabled and option 82 insertion is configured. A DHCP request arrives on an untrusted port already carrying option 82. What does the switch do?
explanation: Option 82 records the relay agent and port that injected it. A client-side untrusted port must not supply it, so a packet that already carries option 82 on an untrusted port is treated as spoofed and dropped. Trusted ports and the switch's own insertion are the legitimate ways for the field to appear.

choices.text: It drops the packet, because option 82 from an untrusted source is not allowed
It replaces the existing option 82 with its own and forwards the packet
It forwards the packet unchanged to the DHCP server
It strips option 82 and forwards the request

stem: Why is `snmp-server ifindex persist` configured on a switch?
explanation: Interface indexes are normally assigned at boot and can change after a reload, which would make an NMS attribute old data to a different port. Persisting them writes the mapping to NVRAM so the ifIndex values a poller already knows stay valid. The command says nothing about communities, engine IDs, or counters.

choices.text: To keep each interface's ifIndex stable across reboots so the NMS does not misattribute collected data
To save SNMP community strings in NVRAM
To fix the SNMP engine ID for version 3
To write interface counters to flash before a reload

stem: Which AAA command records the privileged-level commands an administrator runs, including when each one started and stopped?
explanation: `aaa accounting commands 15` logs command execution at privilege level 15, and `start-stop` sends a start record before the command and a stop record after it, which captures duration. `accounting exec` covers login sessions rather than individual commands, and authentication and authorization do not produce accounting records.

choices.text: `aaa accounting commands 15 default start-stop group tacacs+`
`aaa authentication commands 15 default group tacacs+`
`aaa authorization commands 15 default group tacacs+`
`aaa accounting exec default start-stop group tacacs+`

stem: Which transport and port does RESTCONF use?
explanation: RESTCONF is the HTTP-based model-driven interface and rides HTTPS on TCP 443, with JSON or XML payloads. NETCONF is its SSH-based sibling on TCP 830. Plain HTTP on 80 is not the standard secure default.

choices.text: HTTPS over TCP 443
SSH over TCP 22
HTTP over TCP 80 only
NETCONF over TCP 830

stem: An AIOps tool baselines interface utilisation over a fixed 24-hour window. Every Monday morning it raises false anomalies. What is the flaw?
explanation: A one-day baseline learns only the daily pattern, so a recurring weekly peak falls outside it and looks anomalous. A baseline has to span the period over which behaviour actually repeats, a week or a month, so scheduled peaks become part of normal. Fixed thresholds are the thing baselining is meant to replace.

choices.text: The baseline must cover a full business cycle, such as a week, so recurring weekly peaks count as normal
The window is too long and therefore hides real incidents
Interface utilisation cannot be baselined statistically
The tool should use a fixed threshold instead of a baseline

stem: An agent automatically retries a failed tool call. Why should the tool be idempotent?
explanation: If the first call actually succeeded but its response was lost, the retry must not create a second VLAN or a duplicate ticket. An idempotent tool leaves the system in the same state no matter how many times it is invoked, which is what makes an automatic retry safe. Speed, argument validation, and provider-side caching are unrelated concerns.

choices.text: So a repeated call leaves the system in the same state instead of applying the change twice
So the tool returns faster on the second attempt
So the model can skip validating the arguments
So the call can be cached by the model provider

stem: A long prompt places a critical formatting rule in the middle of thousands of tokens of reference material. The model follows the rule only some of the time. What is the most likely explanation?
explanation: This is the lost-in-the-middle effect: recall for content in the middle of a long context is measurably worse than for content at the start or the end. Restating the rule near the top or the bottom, or moving it into the system message, is the usual fix. If the context window were exceeded the request would fail outright rather than degrade intermittently.

choices.text: Models attend most reliably to the beginning and end of a context, so a rule buried in the middle is often missed
The rule is too short to be tokenized correctly
The model's context window is smaller than the prompt
The rule contradicts the system message
